knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Ratios

question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $s=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{19}\right)$ and $c=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{19}\right)$. The **double-angle formula** gives $\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{19}\right)=2sc$.

 The reciprocal definition gives $\csc\left(\frac{\pi}{19}\right)=\frac{1}{s}$.

Expand the doubled sine and cancel the common factor.

$$
\begin{aligned}
2sc\frac{1}{s} &=\frac{2sc}{s} \\ &=2c \\ &=2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{19}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

All cancellations use nonzero factors in the original expression.

generation.domain: Original denominators and reciprocal functions must be defined; sampled angles are acute and nonspecial.
